engine: A plain CPython subprocess on the host (sys.executable on a temp file), started with a copy of the host environment. No sandbox.
how_run: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor(work_dir=tmp, functions=[lookup]).execute_code_blocks([CodeBlock(language='python', code=...)]), the call CodeExecutorAgent makes. Guest code imports the tool with `from functions import lookup`.

P1.detail: Printed 42. 0 host-side calls: the executor copies lookup's source into functions.py (_common.py:52-67) and the guest imports it, so the tool body ran once inside the executor subprocess (1 LOOKUP_CALL marker on its stderr). There is no host bridge.

P2.detail: All 200000 printed chars came back, no truncation marker. The bare last expression is not returned: the result is only stderr + stdout text (local/__init__.py:458-459).

P5.detail: ENV=s3cr3t. The subprocess gets env = os.environ.copy() (local/__init__.py:397).

P6.detail: Stopped at 60.2 s: exit_code=124 "Timeout" (default timeout=60). Caveat measured in out/P6-orphan.txt: a guest that starts a child holding stdout (sleep 37) and then loops made execute_code_blocks return only after 37.0 s with timeout=10, because asyncio's proc.wait() waits for the pipes to close. A child that never exits would block the call indefinitely.

P7.detail: No memory limit. The guest subprocess grew to 4.46 GB RSS and the harness killed it. The harness process (the host) survived because the guest is a separate process.

P8.detail: Variables are fresh (each block is a new python process). Files persist: a file written by one execution was read back by the next (out/PX.txt, P8-files).

defaults.time: timeout=60 s per code block (local/__init__.py:39 and :149), enforced with asyncio.wait_for then proc.terminate() (:441-448). A child process holding stdout keeps the call blocked past the timeout (out/P6-orphan.txt).
defaults.output: None. stderr then stdout, concatenated, uncapped (:458-459). 200000 chars came back whole.
defaults.tool_calls: No cap and no host bridge: functions run inside the executor process.

source_notes.finding: Each function's source is copied with inspect.getsource into <work_dir>/functions.py, plus its declared global imports; the guest imports it like any module. Prompt stubs come from to_stub(): the signature and docstring with a `...` body.

All upfront. format_functions_for_prompt() renders every stub into FUNCTION_PROMPT_TEMPLATE. It is marked Experimental and nothing in autogen-agentchat calls it outside tests, so the application has to put it in the prompt itself.
None. The "tool" is code inside the executor, so anything the function needs (API clients, keys) must exist in the executor process. Locally that is the host's whole environment.

None. The code runs as a host subprocess with os.environ.copy() and cwd=work_dir. The class docstring says command-line code "is sanitized using regular expression match against a list of dangerous commands"; no such code exists in the executor (grep for sanitize finds only the docstring). The constructor warns that it executes code on the local machine and recommends Docker.
Only text: stderr followed by stdout, no return value, no truncation.
timeout (default 60, minimum 1) is the only limit. On timeout the direct child gets SIGTERM; grandchildren are not killed, and await proc.wait() then waits for their pipes.
Fresh interpreter per code block. The work_dir (a TemporaryDirectory by default) persists across blocks, so files are shared state.
Non-zero exit code plus the raw traceback text from stderr.

The repository is archived and in maintenance mode; the README advises against production use and points to Microsoft Agent Framework. CodeExecutorAgent has an optional approval_func called before each execution. Function requirements are pip-installed into the executor's interpreter at setup.

surprises: The class docstring promises regex sanitization of dangerous commands (local/__init__.py:57-58). No sanitization code exists.

`functions` is not a tool bridge: the function's source is copied into the sandbox and executed there, so host call counts are 0 and any credential the tool needs has to live where the model's code runs.
The timeout does not bound the call when the guest leaves a child holding stdout: timeout=10 returned after 37.0 s (out/P6-orphan.txt).
microsoft/autogen is archived; its README calls AutoGen research software and advises against production use.
